solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Crooks casing large compounds (6)

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so BENDS wraps round L

blocks.note: crooks = bends, as in the crook of an arm

annotation.surface: Criminals are hiding out in big fortified compounds.
annotation.walkthrough: "Crooks" wants to be villains and "compounds" a walled enclosure; both are verbs-turned-nouns in disguise, bends and mixtures.
annotation.definitionFit: A blend is a mixture of things, which is what a compound is.

entries.clue: Insect circles as bird regularly skipped by (6)

indicators.note: to circle something is to surround it, so BEE goes round SID
letters skipped at regular intervals leave every other one

blocks.note: every second letter of A S B I R D

annotation.surface: A bug and a bird circle each other, the bird flitting past now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last little word: "by" in the sense of next to. The bird is not a bird at all, just letters to thin out.
annotation.definitionFit: Beside and by both mean next to, as in a house by the sea.

entries.clue: Politician overcoming resistance in effort for immunity (9)

indicators.note: the MP overcomes, pushing out and taking the place of, the R

blocks.note: R = resistance, the physics symbol; this is the letter removed
MP = Member of Parliament; this goes in where R was

annotation.surface: A politician struggles against opposition while trying to win legal immunity.
annotation.walkthrough: Start from EXERTION and swap its R for MP. "Politician" and "immunity" together suggest parliamentary privilege, which is exactly the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: An exemption frees you from a rule or duty, which is what immunity does.

entries.clue: Hellish music from unsigned artist, pleasant when cut short (7)

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a demo is the recording a band without a label sends out
NICE with its final E cut off

annotation.surface: A review: the unsigned band's hellish racket would be pleasant if only it were shorter.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hellish music" reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at "Hellish"; the music belongs to the demo tape.
annotation.definitionFit: Demonic means of or like demons, hence hellish.

entries.clue: Unexpected communication from officer beginning to disperse around everyone (4,4)

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its first letter

blocks.note: C = circa, Latin for around, as in c. 1900

annotation.surface: An officer sends a surprise order for everyone to scatter.
annotation.walkthrough: "Around" looks like a container instruction but is just C, circa. The officer is a colonel, not a CO.
annotation.definitionFit: A cold call is a sales call nobody was expecting.

entries.clue: Take away tips from frank individuals (4)

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters, which go

blocks.note: frank = honest; lose the H and T at either end

annotation.surface: Remove the advice given by blunt people.
annotation.walkthrough: "Take away" suggests a meal or subtraction and "tips" advice or gratuities; here they strip the ends off HONEST.
annotation.definitionFit: Ones are single units, as in taking them one by one: individuals.

entries.clue: Wow! Edam and rye crackers (5,2)

indicators.note: crackers means mad, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: Someone is delighted by a cheese board of Edam and rye crackers.
annotation.walkthrough: Crackers sits right next to cheese, so it reads as biscuits; it is the anagram signal, meaning mad. "And" is not fodder here: the letters come from Edam and rye.
annotation.definitionFit: Deary me is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, like wow.

entries.clue: Listened to a smarter lady (5)

indicators.note: what is heard, not seen, gives the answer

blocks.note: neater = smarter, as in tidier; run 'a neater' together and it gives a woman's name

annotation.surface: Someone paid attention to a cleverer woman.
annotation.walkthrough: "Smarter" means tidier, not cleverer. Crosswords often let "lady" or "girl" stand for any woman's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Anita is a woman's name, and a lady stands for one.

entries.clue: Ears bear piercings (8)

blocks.note: to lug = to bear, carry something heavy

annotation.surface: Someone's ears carry piercings.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bear" is a verb, not the animal. Lughole is British slang for ear.
annotation.definitionFit: Lugholes is a jokey British word for ears.

entries.clue: Each male in animal enclosure is amorous (6)

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the enclosure

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

annotation.surface: Each boar in the pigpen is feeling frisky.
annotation.walkthrough: The farmyard picture holds, but the answer is the mood, not the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: steam suggests heat, and heat suggests passion.

entries.clue: Chilling unknown exotic lager in bottles (8)

indicators.note: exotic means foreign and unusual, so the letters are rearranged
to bottle something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: the seven letters of LAGER IN, rearranged
X = an unknown, as in algebra

annotation.surface: Someone is cooling an unfamiliar foreign lager in bottles.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chilling" suggests a fridge, and the beer keeps up the idea; it means taking it easy.
annotation.definitionFit: To chill is slang for to relax.

entries.clue: Conifers planted in bit of turf reflected stupidity (8)

indicators.note: the trees are set into the turf
a mirror image reads backwards

blocks.note: a sod is a piece of turf

annotation.surface: Planting pine trees in a scrap of lawn showed poor thinking.
annotation.walkthrough: "Reflected" applies only to the bit of turf; the conifers read forwards and are planted inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Dopiness is being dopey, slow-witted: stupidity.

entries.clue: Asset abroad concealing name is most sensible (6)

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters wander
the anagram hides N inside it

annotation.surface: Keeping one's name off an overseas asset is the wisest move.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an offshore tax dodge; "abroad" only tells you to mix up ASSET.
annotation.definitionFit: Sanest is the superlative of sane, and sane means sensible.

entries.clue: Energetic person involved in too many deeds to recall (6)

indicators.note: the answer is caught up inside the words that follow
to recall is to call back, so read backwards

blocks.note: tO MANY Deeds, read right to left

annotation.surface: A go-getter has done too many things to remember them all.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a busy person's diary, which is exactly what the answer is.
annotation.definitionFit: A dynamo is literally a generator, figuratively a person full of energy.

entries.clue: Frenchman‘s blunder filling pastry (6)

indicators.note: the mistake is the pie's filling, sitting inside it

annotation.surface: A French chef's mistake is in his pie filling.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's means "has": Frenchman has blunder filling pastry. Any common French man's name will do as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Pierre is a typical French man's name.

entries.clue: Uncaring leaders in institute newly swindle with bank fee (13)

indicators.note: the leading letters of the next words

blocks.note: first letters of Institute and Newly
a bank is the side of a river
a rate is a fee, as in an hourly rate

annotation.surface: Heartless bosses at a new institute rip people off with bank charges.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bank fee" reads as one banking charge; split it, since the bank is a riverbank.
annotation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate means not thinking of others: uncaring.

entries.clue: Article amused an eccentric endlessly (2,7)

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A newspaper piece kept an odd person entertained for ages.
annotation.walkthrough: "Article" looks like a newspaper story; it is the grammar word giving A. The anagram covers only "amused an".
annotation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for to the point of sickness, used to mean endlessly.

entries.clue: Singer from Tottenham accepts help somewhere in Australia (8)

indicators.note: the singer takes the help inside her

blocks.note: Adele grew up in Tottenham, north London

annotation.surface: A London pop star agrees to help out at a gig Down Under.
annotation.walkthrough: Tottenham is a district of north London, best known for its football club, but here it pins down the singer Adele.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the city is one place in Australia, the capital of South Australia.

entries.clue: Get an old nurse to train healthcare worker (6,7)

indicators.note: to train something is to shape it, so the letters are reworked

annotation.surface: Hire a veteran nurse to teach a medical trainee.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue sits in a hospital, and "nurse" pulls towards a nursing answer, but it is the dentist from the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon is a dentist, who works in healthcare.

entries.clue: American left-wing student group turned into fragmented parts (7)

indicators.note: turned round, so read backwards

blocks.note: the NUS is the UK's National Union of Students

annotation.surface: A radical campus group in the US has splintered into factions.
annotation.walkthrough: Only RED plus NUS is reversed; the A stays at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart, into pieces, as in torn asunder.

entries.clue: Former husband of countess that is close to her (7)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a countess is the wife of an earl

annotation.surface: A countess's ex-husband is still close to her.
annotation.walkthrough: "Former husband" reads as ex-husband, but the definition is just "Former"; the husband is the earl.
annotation.definitionFit: Former and earlier both mean coming before.

entries.clue: Debt is rent for accommodation (6)

indicators.note: rent here means torn apart, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A tenant's money trouble is the rent owed on their lodgings.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rent" is the past tense of rend, torn. A bedsit is British for a single rented room used for sleeping and living.
annotation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a one-room flat, a kind of accommodation.

entries.clue: Group leaves guests, both half-cut (6)

indicators.note: each of the two words loses half its letters

annotation.surface: A party of revellers walks out, with guests and hosts all tipsy.
annotation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, which is the party picture; here it means cut in half.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: teams or allies banded together form a group.

entries.clue: Own hands moist, now and again (5)

indicators.note: only some of the time, so every other letter

annotation.surface: Someone's palms get sweaty every so often.
annotation.walkthrough: "Own" is the verb, as in own up.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: owning a fault, or owning up to it, means confessing it.

entries.clue: Again, move back beside Yorkshire river (8)

annotation.surface: Someone moves back once more to live beside a river in Yorkshire.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is split: "Again" and "move", in the sense of stir the feelings. "Move back" wants to be one instruction, but back is the REAR.
annotation.definitionFit: Arouse can mean move or stir the feelings, and the RE- prefix supplies the again.

entries.clue: Like upcoming commercial for supermarket (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top

annotation.surface: A trailer for a forthcoming supermarket advertisement.
annotation.walkthrough: Asda is a large British supermarket chain. "Upcoming" looks like next week's ad; it reverses AD.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a large British grocery chain, like Tesco or Sainsbury's.

entries.clue: Getting round backtracking editor, this writer’s very cocky (8)

indicators.note: the word gets round, surrounds, the reversed editor
going back over its tracks, so read backwards

blocks.note: this writer = I, the setter; this writer's = I'm
most = very, as in most kind

annotation.surface: A writer boasts of dodging an editor who wants to backtrack.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter speaks as "this writer", giving I'M, which goes at the front, not round anything.
annotation.definitionFit: Cocky means immodest, too sure of oneself.

entries.clue: Those sorting things when king’s involved in difficulties (6)

indicators.note: the king is caught up inside the difficulties

blocks.note: to be in a fix is to be in difficulty

annotation.surface: Aides who sort problems out when the monarch gets into trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: A royal trouble-shooter is the answer the surface paints, and that is what it is.
annotation.definitionFit: Fixers are people who sort things out.

entries.clue: Foreign lover once learnt to adapt (8)

indicators.note: to adapt something is to change it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an ex is a former lover

annotation.surface: A foreign ex-partner once learnt to fit in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Foreign lover" reads as one person, but "Foreign" alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: External means from outside, which is one sense of foreign, as in a foreign body.

entries.clue: Timely training following school function (6)

indicators.note: the training comes after, following, the school function

blocks.note: a prom is a school dance

annotation.surface: Rehearsals come in good time after the school dance.
annotation.walkthrough: "School function" might suggest a maths function or an assembly; it is a dance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something done promptly happens at just the right time.
